full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This Rule Nisi has been issued on an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents should not be directed to implement the recommendation made by the Sick Industries Rehabilitation Cell in its report dated 25-8-1992 (Annexure-D-3) and rehabilitate the petitioner's sick industry and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna in Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 42 of 2000 (Annexure-I and I-1) and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Respondent No. 6, Janata Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 42 of 2000 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna claiming an amount of Taka 20,89,28,042.00 against the defendant-petitioner. The defendant petitioner duly appeared and filed a written statement denying the claim all together. The learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna on consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit on contest against the defendant petitioner by the impugned Judgment and decree dated 9-8-2003 (decree signed on 13-812003). 

 4. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 6 Janata Bank, on the other hand, contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed in the course of argument has taken us through the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition along with annexures as filed therewith and then argues with force that the writ petition is not maintainable against the Judgment and Decree of Artha Rin Adalat. The learned Advocate to fortify this branch of his argument has relied on the decisions namely the decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, 54 DLR (AD)6, 59 DLR (AD) 6. 

 7. We have studied the cited decisions namely the decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, 54 DLR (AD) 6, and 59 DLR (AD) 6. In those decisions, we find our Appellate Division clearly spelt out that since there being special provision for appeal in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain no application under Article 102 of the Constitution lies against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. 

 8. In view of the above well settled principle of law as to the question of maintain-ability of the Writ Petition, we have no hesitation to hold that the petitioner has miserably failed to cross the first hurdle, inasmuch as Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is a special law and special provision having been provided in Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for preferring appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. In order to save the valuable public time since the petitioner could not cross the first hurdle, we do not think it wise to advert all the grounds of the writ petition.
